critical_code_review_comments: Sidebar.jsx canSee() has a fallback for legacy users without module_permissions that returns TRUE for every module — reasonable for migration but means any freshly-migrated non-admin user with a NULL module_permissions field will silently see everything. Consider running a one-time backfill script or defaulting to default_modules_for_role(role) on read (server already does this in GET /users but /auth/me does not fill it, so the frontend receives null and falls back to 'show all'). Suggest: /auth/me should return default_modules_for_role(role) when the user document has no module_permissions.

server.py get_current_user returns user['module_permissions'] which may be None; frontend Sidebar.canSee treats None as 'show all' (line 52). If an admin creates a user via API without body, module_permissions gets defaulted, but existing users predating this feature are still null in DB. Minor migration concern.

UtilizadoresPage grp-all/grp-none testids use raw label strings including accents (e.g. 'grp-all-Financeiro', 'grp-all-RH & Salários'). The '&' and spaces are technically valid in data-testid but selectors need escaping. Consider using slugified keys (grp-all-financeiro, grp-all-rh-salarios).
UtilizadoresPage does not validate email format on client side — backend does normalise/lowercase, but a UX hint would help.

TechProtectedRoute (App.js:80) permits admin (role==='admin') into /tech — good. But there's no visible signal to the admin that logout from tech portal returns to /admin rather than login (handled in TechLayout.handleLogout with an isAdminViewing branch — nice).

Backend create_user filters modules to only valid ALL_MODULES keys — good defensive coding. But there's no minimum-length password validation (accepts test1234, or even '1'). Consider adding a length check on UserCreate.password.
get_users skips password_hash via projection (good), but users list is capped at 100 with .to_list(100) — reasonable for now.

The consulta role default includes 'propostas: True' (line 3237 server.py) but not 'orcamentos'. Verified via UI — the newly-created consulta user sees Propostas + Negociação (both mapped to propostas mod) in sidebar. Design choice, no bug.
